title: Understanding the Dayli ICC Management Example
hook: Don’t memorize my dollar amount. Understand my risk structure.

launchpad.outcome: Read the 30/60 MNQ example as a structure: points stay put, dollar exposure changes with contracts.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What changes when I change the size?

slides.title: Change the contracts. Watch what moves.
slides.note: These numbers are examples from the Dayli ICC MNQ framework being taught in the Academy. They are not universal numbers for every futures product, account size, or trader.

asks.prompt: 2 MNQ. What’s the risk and reward?
5 MNQ. What’s the risk and reward?

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: The stop is still 30 points. The target is still 60.

options.label: Yes: it doubled
options.why: Same setup. Double the dollars. Section 17 starts here.

slides.punch: DON’T MEMORIZE MY DOLLAR AMOUNT. UNDERSTAND MY RISK STRUCTURE.

slides.quote: Points describe the chart. Contracts decide what the chart costs you.

slides.prompt: What does the 30/60 MNQ example teach, if not the numbers?
slides.modelAnswer: The structure: a defined stop and target in points, a 1:2 relationship, and dollar exposure that comes from points × $2 × contracts. The setup stays the same when the size changes; the exposure doesn’t.

remember: Don’t memorize my dollar amount. Understand my risk structure.
